newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU oilseeds crop overcomes drought, output steady.
newsitem.headline: EU oilseeds crop overcomes drought, output steady.

text.p: European Union 1997/98 oilseeds crops should be little changed from last year's volume of 12 to 13 million tonnes, analysts expect.
Drought-induced losses in sunflowerseed would be more than offset by higher rapeseed harvests in regions less prone to weather damage, they said.
"Rainfall in some southern and western European regions arrived too late to compensate for months of drought in early 1997 but area rises will offset the damage done," one said.
"That presupposes the crops get adequate rain, warmth and more daylight sunshine than seen until now in June and July."
"Disastrous losses no longer look likely although at this early stage you cannot rule out heatwaves in France or Spain."
An area forecast from EU oilseeds lobby ANGO still stands at 5.54 million hectares, up by 3.2 percent from 1996 -- a result of lower set-aside and attractive oilseeds prices.
Trader Alfred C Toepfer in Hamburg has forecast a rapeseed crop of 7.7 million tonnes (7.2 million in 1996) and a sunseed crop of 4.1 million (3.9 million), without specifying other oilseeds.
The Oil World newsletter expects 7.79 million tonnes of rapeseed in 1997 (7.11 million in 1996), 3.37 million tonnes of sunseed (3.81 million) and 1.25 million tonnes of soybeans (one million).
The EU also produces a combined maximum of one million tonnes of cottonseed, linseed and pulses.

In France, the farm ministry, broadly in line with industry and independent forecasts, puts the rapeseed area up 8.6 percent at 950,000 ha, sunflower down 0.1 percent at 890,000 ha and soybeans up 7.9 percent at 93,000 ha.
Of the 1.93 million ha total, oilseeds for food use extend to 1.7 million ha, according to Antoine Morin, a crop analyst for oilseeds industry group FOP.
Trader Bernard Nicol sees the rapeseed crop rising only to three million tonnes from 2.95 million tonnes in 1996.
He cites yields at 3.2 tonnes per hectare (tph), down from 3.4 tph last year after drought and frost in March/April.
Nicol said soybean and sunseed weather was also favourable, and forecast an unchanged sunseed crop of 2.1 million tonnes.
Morin said farmers had raised the soybean area because they had favoured beans over maize while there were acute drought fears in April.
In Italy, the national agricultural research institute ISMEA estimates the soybean area this year will rise by 70,000-100,000 ha over last year's 224,000 ha.
An ISMEA crop expert said the crop should be accordingly higher because drought (mainly in the north) and frost (mainly in the south) had not affected it, other than delaying some sowings.
Spain might harvest 950,000 tonnes of sunflower this year, down 19,000 tonnes from 1996, Oil World said. The area would be a steady 1.15 million ha but with lower yields of 0.83 tph (1.00 in 1996).
Traders said irrigation had helped counter the effects of drought.
In Britain, a far better rapeseed crop could be harvested after 1.4 million tonnes in 1996 because higher plantings and better plant health should outweigh the impact of drought and frost.
The winter rape area, accounting for more than 80 percent of the expected total, was up by 25.3 percent at 387,200 ha in the December census and farmers expect good yields.
Dutch analyst Stigevo puts Germany's 1997 rapeseed crop at 2.75 million tonnes after just under two million in 1996, citing advances in area and yield and only minor winter damage.
